### Images from British Museum

These images are copyright for British Museum and allowed to be used according to the license determined by them.

To visualize all images, use the left and right arrows on the slide below.

1 / 28
Phoenician text displayed in the British Museum. © Trustees of the British Museum ( ).
Related content:
  • Playing with Consonants and Vowels - An interactive game to understand how syllables are created. ()
2 / 28
Banner in a style similar to that found in Wu Zetian's (武則天) tomb. © Trustees of the British Museum ().
Related content:
  • Wu (武) Family - Family of Empress Wu Zetian (武則天). ()
3 / 28
Babilonia Tablet Babilónico about the flood. © Trustees of the British Museum ().
Related content:
  • Texts with Sciences (Conclusion) - After understanding the water cycle, it is time to investigate catastrophic events linked to this essential resource. ()
  • Literature and science - it is not uncommon to hear that a text represents the truth, but what is truly true about that? ()
  • Texts with Sciences (Part III) - With everything we have learned, what conclusions can we draw from ancient texts that discuss deluges? ()
4 / 28
The Flood Tablet. © Trustees of the British Museum ().
Related content:
  • Sui Dynasty (隋代) - the dynasty that unified the region, allowing great advances in Chinese civilization. ()
5 / 28
Abydos King List. © Trustees of the British Museum ().
Related content:
  • Texts with Sciences (Conclusion) - After understanding the water cycle, it is time to investigate catastrophic events linked to this essential resource. ()
  • Literature and science - it is not uncommon to hear that a text represents the truth, but what is truly true about that? ()
  • Texts with Sciences (Part III) - With everything we have learned, what conclusions can we draw from ancient texts that discuss deluges? ()
  • Texts with Sciences (Part I) - In the initial texts, we analyzed the relationship between texts and various scientific disciplines, though we have not yet achieved a complete textual interpretation. In this text, we begin exploring ancient Mesopotamian texts with the support of scientific research. ()
  • Sumerians - The Dynasties of Uruk - In this section, we explore various Mesopotamian epics, including the Epic of Gilgamesh. These remarkable works not only reflect the cultural and religious aspects of Sumerian civilization but also convey beliefs and narratives that continue to resonate to this day ()
6 / 28
Different types of vessels, exhibited at the British Museum. © Trustees of the British Museum ( ).
Related content:
  • Cradles of civilization (Parte II) - We continue our study by exploring the civilizations of Egypt, Indus Valley, and China. ()
7 / 28
Cyrus Cylinder. © Trustees of the British Museum ( ).
Related content:
  • The Writing System - More than just a tool for daily use, the writing system is a milestone that allows us to divide human history into prehistory and recorded events. ()
8 / 28
Map of the Inhabited World. © Trustees of the British Museum ().
Related content:
  • Jōmon Period (/ - ) - initial historical period characterized by vessels with cord markings (jōmon). ()
9 / 28
Tablet found in Tell Al-'Ubaid. © Trustees of the British Museum ().
Related content:
  • Shimashki ( - ) - This "lost" kingdom dominated Elam after the fall of Awan. ()
10 / 28
Astrolabe showing a calendar with the months in Latin, held in the British Museum. © Trustees of the British Museum ( ).
Related content:
  • Equality Levels - Some concepts, like the definition of a planet, change over time. Sometimes, objects with slightly different sizes can be considered equal. How can we use numbers to quantify equality? ()
  • Cradles of civilization (Part I) - While humanity originated in Africa, the first civilizations emerged in various regions around the world, such as Mesopotamia, the Andes, and Mesoamerica. ()
  • The Ancient Babylonian World Map - Babylon: Study of the first known world map. ()
  • Texts with Sciences (Part II) - After exploring some figures of speech present in ancient texts, a question arises: what was the context of the Flood? ()
11 / 28
Tang Dynasty coin from the year , at the British Museum. © Trustees of the British Museum ( ).
Related content:
  • Sumerians - First Ur Dynasty - This study examines the First Dynasty of Ur as documented in the Sumerian King List and explores its relationship with the Torah. ()
12 / 28
Epic of Lugalbanda. © Trustees of the British Museum ().
Related content:
  • Organizing time - Many cultures organize time into 7-day weeks and months with varying numbers of days (28/29, 30, or 31). Is this division accurate? ()
13 / 28
Clay tablet with materials for Magan boats. © Trustees of the British Museum ().
Related content:
  • Tang Dynasty (唐代) ( - ) - Nearly 300 years of significant advances, innovations, and possible long-distance trade relations. ()
14 / 28
Dedicatory cone. © Trustees of the British Museum ().
Related content:
  • Sumerians - The Dynasties of Uruk - In this section, we explore various Mesopotamian epics, including the Epic of Gilgamesh. These remarkable works not only reflect the cultural and religious aspects of Sumerian civilization but also convey beliefs and narratives that continue to resonate to this day ()
15 / 28
Glass Beads. © Trustees of the British Museum ().
Related content:
  • Understanding the Multiplication Table (6 and 7) - In this text, we will explore how the Mesopotamian people related to these tables. ()
16 / 28
Cylinder Seal of Meskalamdug. © Trustees of the British Museum ().
Related content:
  • Elamites – Dynasty of Awan - One list mentions three kings who ruled for 356 years (Sumerian King List). Another list presents twelve kings who ruled for about 200 years (List of the Kings of Awan). Why does this discrepancy exist? ()
17 / 28
Vessel decorated with cord marks, exhibited at the British Museum. © Trustees of the British Museum ( ).
Related content:
  • Great Zimbabwe - civilization built by the Shona people, one of the Bantu-speaking groups, in Zimbabwe. ()
18 / 28
Clovis point projectile exhibited at the British Museum. © Trustees of the British Museum ().
Related content:
  • Higher orders with Soroban and Suanpan (算盤) - In this text, we learn how to represent orders higher than the units in the different versions of the abacus. ()
  • Building to count (Suanpan, 算盤) - In this text, we see the differences and what is in common between the Chinese abacus and the Japanese abacus. ()
  • Adding with Soroban, Suanpan (算盤) and Schyoty (счёты) - In this text, we learn how to add with tools developed in Asia. ()
19 / 28
Arrowhead made from bone, featuring inscriptions. © Trustees of the British Museum ( ).
Related content:
  • Sumerians - First Ur Dynasty - This study examines the First Dynasty of Ur as documented in the Sumerian King List and explores its relationship with the Torah. ()
20 / 28
Prism from Library of Ashurbanipal. © Trustees of the British Museum ().
Related content:
  • Our Week - Can We Group the Year Into Weeks? In this text, we explore the calculations made by the Amorites and by ourselves. ()
21 / 28
Pottery exhibited at the British Museum. © Trustees of the British Museum ().
Related content:
  • Jōmon Period (/ - ) - initial historical period characterized by vessels with cord markings (jōmon). ()
22 / 28
Projectile point exhibited at the British Museum. © Trustees of the British Museum ().
Related content:
  • The arrival in Abya Yala (America) ()
23 / 28
Figure of Emperor Xuanzong, exhibited at the British Museum. © Trustees of the British Museum ().
Related content:
  • Tang Dynasty (唐代) ( - ) - Nearly 300 years of significant advances, innovations, and possible long-distance trade relations. ()
24 / 28
Chinese vessel exhibited at the British Museum. © Trustees of the British Museum ().
Related content:
  • The Writing System - More than just a tool for daily use, the writing system is a milestone that allows us to divide human history into prehistory and recorded events. ()
  • Naming - After seeing how we can fill in values between numbers, how about we name them? ()
  • Cradles of civilization (Parte II) - We continue our study by exploring the civilizations of Egypt, Indus Valley, and China. ()
25 / 28
Pottery from Elam, exhibited at the British Museum. © Trustees of the British Museum ().
Related content:
  • Elamites – Dynasty of Awan - One list mentions three kings who ruled for 356 years (Sumerian King List). Another list presents twelve kings who ruled for about 200 years (List of the Kings of Awan). Why does this discrepancy exist? ()
26 / 28
Example of an abacus used in Russia. © Trustees of the British Museum ().
Related content:
  • Schyoty (счёты), or the vertical abacus - What if the abacus wrote numbers vertically? Well, that abacus exists, and we study it in this text. ()
  • Adding with Soroban, Suanpan (算盤) and Schyoty (счёты) - In this text, we learn how to add with tools developed in Asia. ()
27 / 28
Images of the pyramids of Giza, Egypt. © Trustees of the British Museum ().
Related content:
  • Classifying equality - In this text, we see that classifying is more than comparing things that are exactly alike. ()
  • Equal, same group, or different? - A game to reinforce comparisons: things can be equal, belong to the same group, or be completely different. ()
28 / 28
Images of a stepped pyramid in Saqqara, Egypt. © Trustees of the British Museum ().
Related content:
  • Classifying equality - In this text, we see that classifying is more than comparing things that are exactly alike. ()
  • Equal, same group, or different? - A game to reinforce comparisons: things can be equal, belong to the same group, or be completely different. ()
